title: Add a personal named 'strategy' tag to positions and closed trades
description: Elder ch. 55/56/58/59 all lean on the trader tagging every trade with a personal, named strategy/setup type (his own examples: 'false breakout with a divergence,' 'pullback to value') to later see which of their own setups perform best. Nothing in this app's schema captures this today. This is foundational: backend-trade-apgar depends on it, and the ch.59 idea's 'equity curves segmented by strategy' needs it too. Scope here is just the field and its plumbing, not the Apgar or equity-curve features themselves.

checklist.step: Add a nullable `strategy` string field to PositionIn/PositionOut/PositionORM.
Carry `strategy` through to ClosedTradeORM/ClosedTradeOut when a position is closed (DELETE /api/portfolio/positions/{id}).

Decide free-text vs. a user-managed fixed list of strategies, and record the rationale (Elder's own framing is that strategies are personal and evolve over time -- 'you may develop new strategies and drop others').
Unit/integration tests covering a position created with and without a strategy tag, and that it carries through correctly to the closed-trade row on close.

decisions.decision: `strategy` is free-text, not a user-managed fixed/enum list of strategy names.
decisions.rationale: Elder's own framing (docs/ideas.md's ch. 55/56 entry, quoting the book) is that a trader's named strategies are personal and evolve over time ('you may develop new strategies and drop others') -- a fixed list would need its own CRUD surface (create/rename/retire a strategy) that nothing in this task's scope calls for, and would block tagging a trade with a brand-new strategy the moment it's invented rather than after a separate list-management step. This also matches the existing `entry_notes` field's own free-text precedent (backend-trade-journal-entry-notes task) for the same kind of personal, unstructured trader input on `PositionIn`/`PositionOut`/`ClosedTradeOut`. Downstream consumers that need to group by strategy (the future backend-trade-apgar task, and the ch. 59 'equity curves segmented by strategy' idea) can still group by exact string match on whatever the user has typed -- a fixed list isn't a precondition for that, just a nicer UX a later task could add without changing this field's fundamental shape.

decisions.decision: On `POST /api/portfolio/positions` merging into an existing same-ticker position, an incoming `strategy` *overwrites* the existing tag (if any) rather than being appended to it the way `entry_notes` is. A merge with no incoming `strategy` leaves the existing tag untouched.
decisions.rationale: This deliberately diverges from `entry_notes`' own merge-append convention (backend-trade-journal-entry-notes task), even though the two fields look superficially similar (both nullable free-text strings carried the same way from PositionIn through to ClosedTradeOut). `entry_notes` is a narrative, human-readable note where preserving every buy's own rationale has value and concatenation reads fine. `strategy` is meant to be a single, consistent tag a later feature groups/aggregates on exactly -- the ch. 59 'equity curves segmented by strategy' idea and the future backend-trade-apgar task both need one clean value per trade to bucket by, not a growing concatenation of every strategy ever associated with a ticker's position (e.g. 'Pullback to value\n\nFalse breakout with a divergence' would be its own distinct, never-repeated bucket, defeating the whole point of grouping). Overwriting keeps the field usable for that purpose; rejecting the merge or erroring on a strategy mismatch was considered and rejected as unnecessarily strict for what is otherwise a totally ordinary, always-allowed same-ticker merge (api-portfolio-add-position task's own `decisions`).
